_: The Tools page's cards (tools/make_fm1.py renders web/tools.html's <!--TOOLS--> from it, static for the search engines). Each: name, what (one plain line), by ([name, link], ...), devices, licence, links ([label, url]: the first is the main one), source. Every link checked when added (2026-10-17). "official": the box apart (not open source).

groups.title: Try without a device
groups.sub: Run the firmwares on your computer: nothing installed, nothing touches your FM-1.

tools.name: fm1-emu
tools.what: Emulates the FM-1 and runs its firmwares unchanged: in the browser, as a desktop app, or as an AU / VST3 instrument in your DAW. It loads the hub's firmwares, and has the SMK-37 too.

tools.name: fm1-emulator
tools.what: Emulates the FM-1's chip and board on QEMU and runs the same .fwsc package you would install, with the screen, keys, knobs and sound. A desktop app for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x86-64).

groups.title: Sounds & editors
groups.sub: Edit voices, manage banks, bring your own samples.

tools.name: FM1 Editor & Librarian
tools.what: A DX7 voice editor and patch librarian in the browser: banks, every DX7 parameter and the FM-1's effects, sent over USB MIDI. For the stock firmware and FM-1+VA.

tools.name: Dexed
tools.what: The DX7 as a free plugin and app: edit voices and banks and send them as SysEx. The stock FM-1 takes DX7 SysEx.

tools.name: zp12 sample editor + backup
tools.what: Your own samples on the zp12 firmware: drop a WAV, trim it or chop a loop, hear it as the FM-1 plays it, put it on a pad. And a backup of zp12's loops, sounds, songs and samples.

tools.name: sloopDX editor
tools.what: The sloopDX firmware's editor in the browser: DX7 voices, sounds, sequencer and tracks, .syx bank upload and a backup.

tools.name: FM-1 Workbench (community)
tools.what: A community workbench in the browser: DX7 voice library and editor, a drum sequencer, a MIDI file player and a speech tab, with a software FM-1 when none is connected. Also an Android app and a VST3 / CLAP controller. Not M-VAVE's FM1 Workbench.

groups.title: Backup & rescue
groups.sub: Save the whole flash before you experiment, and bring back an FM-1 that no installer reaches.

tools.name: The hub's Rescue
tools.what: Puts a firmware back on an FM-1 that no installer reaches any more, through the chip's own bootloader. A Python script for Linux.

tools.name: MvaveFM1Unbricker
tools.what: Unbricks an FM-1: first a full flash backup (read twice and compared), then it writes the firmware and checks every byte. Windows and Linux; macOS through the FM-1 Transporter.

tools.name: M-Flasher
tools.what: Backs up, restores and installs firmware through the chip's USB download mode, so it also works when the firmware is broken. Windows, macOS and Linux.

tools.name: FM-1 Transporter
tools.what: Hardware: a Seeed XIAO RP2040 wired to the FM-1's USB lines reads and writes its whole flash, 1 MiB in about three seconds.

groups.title: For developers
groups.sub: Build your own firmware, port one, or look under the hood.

tools.name: Build your own
tools.what: Dinghy is the smallest FM-1 firmware to build on, with the plumbing done and documented. Felucca's BUILDING.md shows how a full firmware is built, and felucca-bsp is the chip and board layer under it.

tools.name: fm1-to-smk37
tools.what: A guide to moving FM-1 firmwares to the SMK-37: what changes, and how the hub's SMK-37 ports were made.

tools.name: Under the hood
tools.what: FM-1-RE: the reverse engineering of the FM-1's firmware and its update protocol. jl-uboot-tool: a flasher and dumper for JieLi chips like the FM-1's.

official.name: M-VAVE FM1 Workbench
official.what: M-VAVE's own editor and simulator in the browser (Chinese or English): play and edit, projects, sounds and samples, and switching the firmware between the official V15 and their Open V13.
official.note: Not open source as a whole: the app is GPL-3.0 with an SDK exception, the sound engine is a closed library. The way back is V15, from the same page.
